chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Isḥ from Isḥaq ibn al-Fadl: that he asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about prostrating on mats and carpets.

He said: 'There is no harm, but for me it is more beloved that he prostrates on the ground, for indeed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) loved that he make his forehead touch the ground. So I love for you what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) loved.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray on carpets and mats in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the fiqh of prostration surfaces, permitting mats and carpets while elevating direct contact with the earth as the preferred Sunnah. He grounds this preference in the Prophet’s specific love for allowing his forehead to rest fully on the ground, thereby linking ritual propriety to the Prophet’s personal aesthetic and spiritual habits. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on emulating the Prophet’s detailed practices (tashabbuh) while maintaining flexibility in worldly matters.
